findings.description: PASS, and the clause's central insight re-derives correctly: the two halves of the rule at SKILL.md:122 really do live in different files, and the clause is right about which file each lives in. Without it a lazy negative fixture passes for the wrong reason — two notes instead of three — and grades nothing about acknowledgement. Requiring three or more on both sides also sidesteps the off-by-one about whether the note being written counts toward the threshold, which the skill leaves open.

findings.description: PASS. All seven acceptance criteria map to at least one blocker clause, and no clause is an orphan. AC1 (fixture, prompt, pass condition per scenario) -> C-2, with C-3 supplying the existence half. AC2 (with and without the skill, delta graded) -> C-4 per scenario, C-12 for the table that records it, C-10 for the second staged copy that makes the baseline run possible at all. AC3 (contradiction round-trip end to end) -> C-5, which names all four artifacts rather than stopping at detection. AC4 (unacknowledged tension its own scenario) -> C-6, both branches. AC5 (scope proposal across three tiers) -> C-7, three tiers plus the tiebreak case. AC6 (nothing written to a real scope) -> C-10, backed by C-11's byte-identity snapshot and C-1's clean diff. AC7 (doc lives beside the other maintainer evals) -> C-1 for the path and C-12 for the shape. The three clauses with no AC of their own are justified rather than orphaned: C-9 guards the failure the spec's own framing implies (an eval that grades against a token the skill does not emit fails correct work), C-11 is the standard regression gate for a repo whose suites walk the fixtures tree, and C-13 applies the user's standing prose requirement to a doc a maintainer will actually read. The non-goals section is consistent with all thirteen and forecloses the two scope creeps this job invites — fixing a skill defect a scenario exposes, and refreshing the two inventories these deliverables make stale.

findings.description: PASS, both shapes. That is closed from four directions at blocker severity — C-5 mandates a contradiction scenario, C-6 a tension scenario with both branches, C-7 three tiers plus a tiebreak case, C-8 a Tier 2 scenario with an unsourced-summary row. A doc satisfying the constitution therefore carries at least six scenarios before C-2 and C-4 have anything to say. The second dodge, a scenario carrying a table of contentless rows, is closed by C-4's transplant test and by C-5/C-7/C-8 naming the specific artifact each table must assert. The third, a run procedure nobody can follow, is closed by C-10's existence gate firing before anything else runs.

findings.description: PASS, no contradictions found, and the citations hold. I resolved every line reference in the document at source: SKILL.md:122, scope-decisions.md:21-25, machine-contracts.md's ten-row table, lint-scope.sh:218-230, and smoke-suite :515, :586, :1226, :1229. All eight land exactly where the clause says they do, which is not something to take on faith in a document on its sixth round. Three pairs that look like collisions and are not. C-9 versus C-5: C-5 mandates `[[<target>|memory — updated]]`, which C-9's token sweep would flag as unregistered — except C-9 strips wiki links first and names C-5 as the reason, so the two are reconciled in the text rather than by luck. C-1 versus C-11: a new fixture turning a suite red cannot be fixed by editing the suite, because tests/ is outside C-1's allowlist; C-11 states that rather than leaving a worker to discover it. C-12 versus C-2: C-12 requires a global `## Fixtures` section while C-2 says a fixture named elsewhere does not satisfy a scenario — the precedent does both (a `## Fixtures` block at :9-12 and a per-scenario `**Repo:**` line), so satisfying both is the normal shape, not a squeeze. Residuals I would have written differently, recorded for Phase 2 checkers and deliberately not converted into findings: (1) C-2's terminal boundary names `## Grading` and is undefined if that section is missing — a state C-12 already fails, but a checker meeting it should report the anomaly rather than silently falling back to end-of-file; (2) neither C-12's text nor its check pins section *order*, which C-2's terminal boundary quietly assumes; (3) C-9's parenthetical 'the shipped lint, which checks the prefix only' is imprecise — lint-scope.sh:232-237 also constrains memory-candidate scope values — though the clause's own failing example forecloses the misreading; (4) C-9's carve-out phrase 'and `_maintenance/inbox-to-memory/EVALS.md` itself (C-1)' means the path token, not the doc's contents, and a checker reading it as the latter would gut a clause whose entire subject is that doc; (5) C-2 says 'a named fixture' in the singular while C-6 and C-7 push toward scenarios carrying two; (6) C-8's 'run `--tier2-extract`' does not name migrate-scope.sh or say whether to stage a copy first — safe either way, since the extract pass refuses to apply; (7) C-8's 'identify the note the scenario grades' leaves a multi-note fixture to checker inference, recoverable by failing those rows as undecidable; (8) C-10's per-run staging requirement, carried in the text with no matching phase in the check. Every one of these is decided correctly by a checker who reads the clause text, which is the standard this document should be held to and not above.
